slide1.headline: China Blocks Meta's $2 Billion AI Deal
slide1.subtitle: Implications for the AI industry

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: China blocked Meta's $2 billion acquisition of AI startup Manus on 28 Apr 2026.
The deal was ordered to be unwound.
Meta had planned to acquire Manus for $2 billion.

slide3.title: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: This decision may impact the growth of AI startups in China.
It could also affect Meta's plans to expand its AI capabilities.
Questions to consider: What will be the impact on Meta's AI strategy? How will this affect the AI industry in China?
Source: Moneycontrol.com, 28 Apr 2026

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: Event date: 13 May 2026
Exaforce, an AI cybersecurity startup, has raised $125 million in funding.
The funding will be used to expand its autonomous security platform.
The company plans to use AI to improve cybersecurity.

slide3.title: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: This funding will help Exaforce to expand its AI-powered cybersecurity solutions.
It could also lead to increased adoption of AI in the cybersecurity industry.
The funding amount of $125 million is significant and indicates the growing interest in AI cybersecurity.

slide4.title: INSIGHTS
bullets: Exaforce's funding is a significant development in the AI cybersecurity space.
The company's autonomous security platform has the potential to revolutionize cybersecurity.
The use of AI in cybersecurity is becoming increasingly important.

slide1.headline: European Commission Draft Guidelines on AI Transparency
slide1.subtitle: Implications for the AI industry

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: Event date: 12 May 2026
The European Commission has released draft guidelines on AI transparency under the EU AI Act.
The guidelines aim to provide clarity on the transparency requirements for AI systems.
The guidelines include 10 key takeaways, including the need for transparency in AI decision-making.

slide3.title: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: These guidelines will have a significant impact on the development and deployment of AI systems in the EU.
They will require companies to be more transparent about their AI decision-making processes.
Questions to consider: How will these guidelines affect the development of AI systems in the EU? What are the implications for companies that use AI in their operations?
Source: Inside Global Tech, 12 May 2026
